papers.title: Vertical characteristics of HCHO and NO 2 in suburban Shanghai: understanding of ozone formation sensitivity via secondary HCHO
papers.authors: Aimon Tanvir, Zeeshan Javed, Shanshan Wang et al.
papers.abstract: Since ozone (O 3 ) pollution in China is on the rise, vertical distribution of nitrogen dioxide (NO 2 ) and formaldehyde (HCHO) and their role towards O 3 formation are critical towards designing O 3 control strategies. Seasonal characteristics of aerosols, HCHO and NO 2 were investigated over suburban Shanghai using multi-axis differential optical absorption spectroscopy from June 2020 to May 2021. For HCHO, the highest average vertical mixing ratios (VMRs) were observed for summer (0.775 ppb), followed by autumn (0.719 ppb), spring (0.718 ppb) and winter (0.672 ppb) at ground level. Seasonal trends in NO 2 VMRs were observed to be opposite to that of HCHO with peak values occurring during winter (2.212 ppb) at the ground level followed by autumn (1.881 ppb), spring (1.415 ppb) and summer (1.124 ppb). In vertical, aerosols depicted a Gaussian shape with a higher values between 0.2–0.5 km. An exponential decay in NO 2 VMRs is observed from 0.0 km to 3.0 km while the integral component of HCHO was found to be concentrated up to 2.0 km particularly during summer months. The vertical distribution of NO 2 in different seasons mainly appeared below 0.5 km, while that of HCHO appeared within the range of 0.2–1.0 km. Both aerosols and NO 2 tend to be higher during haze days compared to non-haze days while HCHO was found to be higher during non-haze days owing to high photochemical activity on a clear day. Based on the ratio of HCHO to NO 2 (RFN), this study attempted to quantify the vertical characteristics of O 3 sensitivity for different seasons. The results indicated that the O 3 sensitivity was VOC-limited both at lower (generally, 0.0–0.6 km) and higher heights (1.8–3.0 km) while some transition limited scenarios were found at middle height (0.7–1.7 km) particularly during daytime. The results depicted that secondary HCHO is a crucial factor controlling on O 3 sensitivity over Shanghai where enhanced ratio of VOC limited regime was observed with secondary HCHO for all the seasons.

papers.title: Within-fire estimates of biomass loss across national forests of the US West Coast: inventory-informed inference with uncertainty
papers.authors: Elliot S. Shannon, Andrew O. Finley, Paul B. May et al.
papers.abstract: Wildfire is reshaping forests in the western United States (US), yet estimates of wildfire impacts often rely on burned-area summaries or satellite-derived severity metrics that do not directly quantify changes in forest biomass or their uncertainty. We combine US Forest Inventory and Analysis plot measurements with annual 30 m tree canopy cover data in a Bayesian spatio-temporal modeling framework to estimate within-fire changes in live aboveground biomass (AGB) and forest mortality area across National Forest System lands in Washington, Oregon, and California. The model represents both live forest presence or absence and AGB conditional on live forest, allowing posterior predictive estimates of pre- and post-fire conditions at the pixel scale. Applied to 6,308 fire analysis areas from 2000 to 2022, the analysis estimates 117.8 million Mg of wildfire-associated AGB loss and 2.98 million ha of forest mortality area, with the largest aggregate impacts occurring in 2020. Pixel-level estimates reveal substantial spatial heterogeneity within fire perimeters, including large differences between total burned area, forest mortality area, and associated biomass loss. This inventory-informed, uncertainty-aware approach provides a scalable framework for quantifying forest carbon impacts of disturbance across broad regions while retaining within-fire spatial detail.

papers.title: Delayed seasonal march of East Asian summer monsoonal rain belt during Heinrich Stadials
papers.authors: Jinzhe Zhang, Ting Wei, Chuncheng Guo, Qing You Yan
papers.abstract: Abstract The timing and duration of monsoon rainfall shape regional hydroclimate, yet their response to abrupt climate change remains poorly constrained. Here, we use 25-km-resolution climate simulations to investigate the seasonal migration of the East Asian summer monsoon rain belt during Heinrich Stadials, periods associated with collapsed Atlantic meridional overturning circulation (AMOC). We find that the rain belt migrated northward 18 days later than during interstadials. This delay kept the monsoon front longer over central China, prolonging early-summer rainfall despite an overall weaker monsoon. The delayed migration was linked to later northward advances of the western North Pacific subtropical high and upper-level westerly jet. North Atlantic cooling contributed to these circulation changes through Rossby wave propagation and a weakened land–sea thermal contrast. Our results suggest that abrupt Atlantic changes can reshape both the amount and seasonal timing of East Asian summer rainfall. These findings offer a palaeoclimate perspective on potential changes in monsoon seasonality under future AMOC weakening.

papers.title: Enhanced coupling between the North Atlantic oscillation and Pacific-North American patterns in a warmer climate
papers.authors: Qi Tian, Hyacinth C. Nnamchi, Jianping Li et al.
papers.abstract: The North Atlantic Oscillation (NAO) and Pacific-North American (PNA) patterns are the most prominent atmospheric teleconnections over the Northern Hemisphere, which are traditionally considered independent of each other. Here we use reanalysis and state-of-the-art climate models to show the emergence of unprecedented coupling between the NAO and PNA in recent decades. This enhanced coupling primarily arises from non-uniform global warming associated with Arctic amplification, which weakens the meridional temperature gradient between the tropics and Arctic. The consequent poleward shift of the midlatitude westerlies displaces PNA’s downstream centers eastward into the North Atlantic region associated with the NAO. Future projections indicate that the NAO-PNA coupling will further strengthen under elevated anthropogenic forcing. These findings reveal a critical impact of climate change on atmospheric teleconnections, reshaping our understanding of the NAO-PNA relationship and its influence on Northern Hemisphere weather extremes.

papers.title: Strategic cropland retirement can achieve groundwater sustainability and biodiversity co-benefits while minimizing economic impacts under climate change
papers.authors: Maxwell Pepperdine, Stella Wing, Harry Scott Butterfield et al.
papers.abstract: Groundwater overdraft and climate change are driving large-scale agricultural land retirement across the world’s water-stressed farming regions, but the hydrologic, ecological, and economic outcomes of retirement depend heavily on where it occurs. Using the San Joaquin Valley, California, as a case study, we identify least-cost spatial configurations of cropland retirement that simultaneously meet groundwater and species habitat goals. We constructed species distribution models, estimated field-level applied water and foregone agricultural revenue, and used mixed-integer linear programming (prioritizr) to solve water-only, habitat-only, and combined (water + habitat) retirement optimizations for present and future scenarios, solving the water-only framework at both regional and individual groundwater basin scales. Our results show that meeting regional overdraft reduction targets required retiring roughly 326,000 ha of cropland at approximately $1.44B in foregone revenue under baseline conditions, rising to about 367,000 ha ($1.60B) under a high-emissions scenario. Regional planning met targets at approximately 4.6% less area and 18.5% lower cost than basin-by-basin planning, revealing a trade-off between regional efficiency and local feasibility in achieving long-term groundwater sustainability. The land needed to meet overdraft reduction goals contained far more suitable habitat than the conservation targets required (170–1298% of each target), indicating significant potential for habitat co-benefits when water-driven retirement was spatially coordinated. Our results do not suggest the retirement configurations as a prescriptive design, but rather as a demonstration of a generalizable spatial planning framework for identifying portfolios that balance irrigation reductions with conservation co-benefits and economic efficiency under climate uncertainty.

papers.title: Antecedent drought exposure weakens vegetation decline without promoting recovery
papers.authors: Shijun Zheng, Le Yu, Zhenrong Du et al.
papers.abstract: Repeated drought can alter vegetation responses to subsequent water stress, but whether reduced canopy decline is accompanied by improved recovery remains unresolved. We analysed global leaf area index and meteorological drought records for 1982–2020 using an event-based framework that separately quantified detectable declines in canopy leaf area, standardized leaf-area losses and recovery to pre-drought conditions. Antecedent drought frequency and cumulative severity were evaluated over five historical windows spanning 12–60 months, alongside the interval since the previous drought. After adjustment for current-drought characteristics and environmental conditions, greater antecedent frequency and severity were associated with lower odds of a clear negative LAI response and smaller losses across all five windows. In contrast, associations with recovery were weak and inconsistent across exposure windows. For the 60-month frequency measure, adjusted predictions from zero to six prior events indicated decreases of 3.7 percentage points in response probability and 0.15 standard deviations in leaf-area loss, while modelled recovery probability within 24 months decreased by only 0.8 percentage points. Associations differed among vegetation groups and forest types, with smaller losses accompanying either faster or slower recovery. Baseline adjustment and recovery sensitivity analyses broadly supported this separation between decline and recovery. These modest observational associations do not establish adaptation or a specific ecological memory mechanism. They show that muted canopy decline alone is insufficient evidence of improved drought resilience and support evaluating impact and recovery separately when assessing vegetation responses to recurrent drought.

papers.title: Lived experiences of people affected by the 2024 spring flood disaster in Kazakhstan: a phenomenological study
papers.authors: Dias Baiseitov, Jonas Preposi Cruz, Ejercito Mangawa Balay‐odao
papers.abstract: This study describes the lived experiences of people affected by the 2024 spring flood disaster in the Republic of Kazakhstan. It utilises a descriptive phenomenological qualitative research design and Canadian scholar Max Van Manen's data analysis approach. The pool of participants comprises 13 individuals who experienced flooding in the country's Aktobe Region, pinpointed through referral sampling. Semi-structured interviews were used to collect the data and the researchers ensured rigour and trustworthiness throughout the project. Initially, 183 codes were identified in the analysis. These were then summarised by meaning, yielding 13 subthemes that were further categorised into four themes: (i) Disrupted Lifeworld: Displacement, Loss, and Disruption of Everyday Life; (ii) Emotional and Existential Consequences of Disaster and Displacement; (iii) Experiencing Social and Institutional Relationships During Recovery; and (iv) Reconstructing Life: Coping, Agency, and Adaptation. The study underscores the need to refine disaster response mechanisms from multiple perspectives, encompassing personal resilience and more effective policies. The disaster in Kazakhstan affected people's intrapersonal relationships and their mental and material well-being.

papers.title: Hidden and fragmented patterns of morphological informality across African cities revealed by open geospatial data
papers.authors: Wenbin Zhang, Weixuan Fang, Alessandro Sorichetta et al.
papers.abstract: Informal settlements are a major yet poorly measured form of urbanization, particularly where small or fragmented clusters are embedded within otherwise formal urban fabric. Here, we develop a scalable geospatial framework for mapping morphological informality across African cities using open satellite imagery, global building data, and eight city-specific machine-learning models combined by equal averaging. Applied to all 84 African cities with projected populations exceeding one million in 2025, the framework generates 10 m probability surfaces. Mean leave-one-city-out F1 at training-selected thresholds was 0.876; independent validation using 1910 reference points yielded AUC of 0.972. Building-presence profiles were the leading SHAP contributor in all eight held-out cities, with height and spectral context providing additional signals. These results support retaining neighborhood building distributions alongside vertical structure and vegetation when mapping across diverse urban contexts. The share of selected area in patches smaller than 1 km 2 increased from 38.0% at p ≥ 0.2 to 72.4% at p ≥ 0.8. WorldPop 2023 allocated fewer people than community-reported counts in 89.0% of 308 settlement polygons, with a median WorldPop/community ratio of 0.263. Community records span 2013–2020, so the comparison diagnoses allocation discrepancies and motivates assessing settlement-specific population densities using contemporaneous evidence. The probability surfaces describe physical morphology, not tenure or household deprivation. Together, the findings identify shared morphological signals and population-allocation discrepancies that can guide local validation, surveys and future population modelling.

papers.title: Climate change adaptation in the Philippines: a systematic review of empirical evidence
papers.authors: Henry Antoine Bartelet, Luisa Fernanda Bedoya Taborda
papers.abstract: Highly climate-vulnerable countries face the dual challenge of responding to growing climate hazards while addressing the social and institutional conditions that shape vulnerability and adaptation. National evidence syntheses are needed to assess how adaptation research is progressing and whether it provides evidence about the outcomes of adaptation responses. We examine these questions in the Philippines, where climate exposure intersects with livelihood precarity, social vulnerability, and uneven institutional capacity. We conducted a systematic review of empirical evidence on human climate change adaptation in the Philippines and identified 99 relevant studies published between 2010 and 2024. We analysed their research themes and empirical findings, together with the subset directly assessing adaptation outcomes or effectiveness. The literature predominantly examines perceptions, adaptive capacity, and sectoral responses, particularly in fisheries, coastal settings, and agriculture. papers.title: Bridging scan-to-BIM and facility management: an IFC-driven framework for information automation in existing buildings
papers.authors: Zicheng Zhu, Kun Tian, Matthew Moorhead, Martin Skitmore
papers.abstract: Facility management (FM) of existing buildings is hindered by fragmented records and Scan-to-BIM models that remain difficult to reuse in operations. This paper presents an IFC-driven framework that transforms four discipline-specific Scan-to-BIM models into a lightweight FM knowledge base and a web-based digital building management system (WDBMS). The framework extracts assets, spaces, storeys, systems, properties, spatial containment, system membership, and MEP port connectivity; normalises them into an FM schema; evaluates information readiness through configurable requirements; and preserves IFC relationship and source-file provenance. Parallel geometry preprocessing produces lightweight web meshes linked to records. The WDBMS integrates a BIM Viewer, Data Workspace, and Knowledge Graph to support bidirectional asset retrieval, validation review, provenance inspection, and topology tracing. The case generated 5345 assets, 90 spaces, 22 storeys, 199 systems, 8091 typed relationships, and 2051 physical connections. This reproducible post-IFC process makes multidisciplinary Scan-to-BIM deliverables queryable, auditable, and operationally accessible.

papers.title: Topology-driven automated generation of geometric digital twins for railway overhead line equipment
papers.authors: M.R. Mahendrini Fernando Ariyachandra, Ioannis Brilakis
papers.abstract: Generating geometric digital twins (GDTs) of railway overhead line equipment (OLE) from point cloud data (PCD) using manual or semi-automated approaches is labour-intensive. This diminishes their practical benefits, with 74% of modelling effort spent converting PCD into GDTs. Automation reduces cost and effort, yet state-of-the-art methods struggle to deliver kilometre-scale GDTs without precision loss or manual intervention. This paper presents an automated method combining topology-aware segmentation, rule-based classification, and template-driven geometric reconstruction. Leveraging engineering rules and OLE spatial relationships, it enables modelling in cluttered, partially occluded scenes. OLE elements are segmented into labelled clusters, then aligned with parametric assemblies to generate industry foundation classes (IFC) models. Evaluation on 18.5 km of PCD achieved F1 scores of 98.3% for C sections, 89.8% for contact and 84.1% for catenary cables, with ±5.6 cm RMSE. Automation saved 98.6% of time versus manual workflows. This contributes a topology-informed strategy for scalable digital twin generation.
